featured.title: Deaf Graduate's AI Alarm SIVO.GO Wins UK James Dyson Award and £5,000
featured.excerpt: Gargi Agrawalla, 23, built SIVO.GO from her own experience of missing alarms with her cochlear implant off; it turns fire alarms and doorbells into light and vibration.
featured.image_caption: Gargi Agrawalla holds the components of SIVO.GO, the AI alert device she designed as her final-year project at Loughborough University. The device won the UK James Dyson Award, carrying a £5,000 prize fund for its next stage of development.
featured.nri_angle: An Indian-origin designer in the UK turned her own experience of deafness into an award-winning safety device — the kind of diaspora engineering story that starts in a dorm room and aims at every hotel room.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: CAA Chief Bryan Lourd Urges Congress to Pass NO FAKES Act Against AI Deepfakes
just_in.excerpt: In a New York Times essay, the head of one of Hollywood's biggest talent agencies argues that the right to refuse an AI replica of your face or voice should be federal law — and that the stalled Senate bill can still pass this year.
just_in.image_caption: CAA chief executive Bryan Lourd, pictured in a Variety photograph.
just_in.nri_angle: A federal consent right over voice and likeness replicas would also protect ordinary families targeted by AI impersonation and scam calls.

just_in.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says He and Claude Have Proven the Riemann Hypothesis
just_in.excerpt: Levent Alpöge's proof exists as 17 million lines of computer-checked code rather than a paper, and the Clay Institute — which offers $1 million for the problem — still lists it as unsolved while review begins.
just_in.image_caption: A plot of the Riemann zeta function, whose non-trivial zeros the Riemann Hypothesis describes. Bernhard Riemann proposed the conjecture in 1859, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers  million for a correct proof.
just_in.nri_angle: A landmark AI research claim from the company many Indian-origin engineers and researchers work for, landing a day after its record Nasdaq debut.

just_in.excerpt: Bloomberg profiles a Google engineer leaving for the UK on a Global Talent visa, and reports employers from IBM to Flywire rethinking US sponsorship as new charges and PERM suspensions stack up.
just_in.image_caption: Yash Sharma, a Google software engineer from India, photographed in San Francisco. Bloomberg profiled Sharma as he prepares to leave the United States for the United Kingdom after six years on an H-1B visa.

just_in.image_caption: SatSure team members in a company portrait. The Bengaluru startup said the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund investment of 600 million rupees forms part of its ongoing 2 billion rupee Series B round.
just_in.nri_angle: Government-backed capital flowing into Indian spacetech is a marker for diaspora investors and professionals watching India's private space sector open up.

just_in.title: Marriage to an Indian Citizen Gives No Right to Stay, Delhi High Court Rules
just_in.excerpt: Dismissing a US citizen's plea to convert her tourist visa into an X-1 spouse visa, Justice Amit Mahajan held that a foreigner's entry and stay are matters of sovereign discretion — and that a marriage certificate does not stop authorities from examining the circumstances.
just_in.image_caption: The emblem of the High Court of Delhi on the court gate in New Delhi, with media cameras gathered outside. The court held that marriage to an Indian citizen does not by itself confer a right to convert a visa into an Entry (X-1) visa or to stay in India.
just_in.nri_angle: Many diaspora families include a foreign-citizen spouse; the ruling confirms that marriage to an Indian citizen is grounds to apply for an X-1 visa, not a right to one.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Malayalam Hits Now Earn a Second Box Office From Diaspora Audiences
just_in.excerpt: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit's ₹136.5 crore overseas gross and record $1.49 million US run show Malayalam cinema's biggest hits are now bankrolled as much abroad as at home.
just_in.image_caption: Nivin Pauly and Mamitha Baiju in a still from Bethlehem Kudumba Unit.

news.title: Heat-Linked Gene Variant Helps Male Malaria Mosquitoes Mate, May Aid Transmission
news.excerpt: A Cell study of Anopheles stephensi, the urban malaria vector native to South Asia, finds a deletion in the timeless clock gene gives males a mating edge in high heat while leaving females easier for the malaria parasite to infect.
news.image_caption: Blood-feeding female Anopheles stephensi mosquitoes. The species, native to South Asia, is the subject of a Cell study linking a timeless-gene variant to heat adaptation and malaria transmission.
news.nri_angle: Anopheles stephensi is the urban malaria mosquito native to India and South Asia, so a heat adaptation that could raise transmission matters for Indian cities and for diaspora families who travel into its range.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Cyclone Akvan: Over 80,000 Evacuated in Odisha as Landfall Nears Friday Noon
news.excerpt: Evacuations have risen past 80,000 against a 2-lakh target, 74 rescue teams are deployed, and the IMD now fixes Akvan's landfall between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, November 20.
news.image_caption: Waves pound a shoreline under grey skies as people watch from the beach, with Cyclone Akvan approaching the Odisha-Andhra coast. Odisha has evacuated more than 80,000 people ahead of the expected landfall on Friday, November 20.
news.nri_angle: Readers with family in coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh face a Friday-noon landfall, with trains and a Chennai–Yangon flight already cancelled or rescheduled.

nri-world.image_caption: World chess champion Gukesh Dommaraju, in the portrait TIME published with its TIME100 Next India list. The 20-year-old appears in the list's Phenoms category, weeks before his first world title defence against Javokhir Sindarov.
nri-world.nri_angle: A New York magazine's first India list, published for a global audience, puts the Chennai world champion in its Phenoms class days before his title defence.

immigration.title: Deported in 1999, Brooklyn Man Can Still Seek Sale of Home Bought in 1985, Court Rules
immigration.excerpt: New York's Appellate Division held that because Clyde Nelson's 2007 divorce never disposed of the Brooklyn house, his ownership share survived — and his former wife cannot use the divorce to block his partition claim.
immigration.image_caption: The Brooklyn skyline in New York. A state appeals court ruled on November 18 that a co-owner removed from the US in 1999 can still seek the sale of a Brooklyn home bought in 1985.
immigration.nri_angle: The ruling shows removal from the US does not erase deed rights, and that a divorce silent on property leaves a deported spouse's share intact.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Senate Bill Asks Labor Department for a Plan on PERM Premium Processing
immigration.excerpt: Appropriators want a report within 60 days of enactment on a fee-based fast track for green card labor certifications that now average about 300 days — but no premium option exists yet.
immigration.nri_angle: PERM is the first green card stage for most H-1B professionals, a heavily Indian cohort; a paid fast track would cut a roughly 300-day wait at the Labor Department stage.

immigration.title: US Proposes PERM Overhaul: 90-Day Job Ads and Layoff Bars for EB-2, EB-3 Sponsors
immigration.excerpt: The Labor Department's first major PERM rewrite in two decades would lengthen recruitment, end the Schedule A bypass and bar sponsors with recent layoffs. It is a proposal only — comments close January 19, 2027, and current rules still apply.
immigration.nri_angle: PERM is the gateway step for most employer-sponsored green cards; Indian H-1B professionals in the EB-2/EB-3 backlog are the group most exposed to longer recruitment and the layoff bar.

immigration.title: H-1B Workers Are Giving Up on US Tech Jobs as Fees and Delays Pile Up
immigration.excerpt: Bloomberg profiles a Google engineer leaving for the UK on a Global Talent visa, and reports employers from IBM to Flywire rethinking US sponsorship as new charges and PERM suspensions stack up.
immigration.image_caption: Yash Sharma, a Google software engineer from India, photographed in San Francisco. Bloomberg profiled Sharma as he prepares to leave the United States for the United Kingdom after six years on an H-1B visa.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders are the largest group exposed to the new fees and PERM suspensions; the open PERM comment window through January 19, 2027 is the one dated action in the story.

immigration.title: Marriage to an Indian Citizen Gives No Right to Stay, Delhi High Court Rules
immigration.excerpt: Dismissing a US citizen's plea to convert her tourist visa into an X-1 spouse visa, Justice Amit Mahajan held that a foreigner's entry and stay are matters of sovereign discretion — and that a marriage certificate does not stop authorities from examining the circumstances.
immigration.image_caption: The emblem of the High Court of Delhi on the court gate in New Delhi, with media cameras gathered outside. The court held that marriage to an Indian citizen does not by itself confer a right to convert a visa into an Entry (X-1) visa or to stay in India.
immigration.nri_angle: Many diaspora families include a foreign-citizen spouse; the ruling confirms that marriage to an Indian citizen is grounds to apply for an X-1 visa, not a right to one.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: After Sikh Grandmother's Deportation, Bill Would Let Old Removal Orders Expire
immigration.excerpt: Four California Democrats introduced the Protect Our Neighbors Act on Thursday, citing Harjit Kaur, 73, who reported to ICE every six months for over 13 years before she was detained at a routine check-in and deported to India.
immigration.nri_angle: The bill responds to the deportation of a Sikh grandmother from California and would directly affect long-term Indian immigrants living in the US under old removal orders.

technology.nri_angle: An Indian-origin designer in the UK turned her own experience of deafness into an award-winning safety device — the kind of diaspora engineering story that starts in a dorm room and aims at every hotel room.

technology.image_caption: CAA chief executive Bryan Lourd, pictured in a Variety photograph.

carousel.title: Deported in 1999, Brooklyn Man Can Still Seek Sale of Home Bought in 1985, Court Rules
carousel.excerpt: New York's Appellate Division held that because Clyde Nelson's 2007 divorce never disposed of the Brooklyn house, his ownership share survived — and his former wife cannot use the divorce to block his partition claim.
carousel.image_caption: The Brooklyn skyline in New York. A state appeals court ruled on November 18 that a co-owner removed from the US in 1999 can still seek the sale of a Brooklyn home bought in 1985.
carousel.nri_angle: The ruling shows removal from the US does not erase deed rights, and that a divorce silent on property leaves a deported spouse's share intact.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Air India Crash Probe in Final Stage, Government Tells Supreme Court
carousel.excerpt: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta sought two to three weeks to finish the AI171 investigation as the court weighs petitions for an independent probe.
carousel.image_caption: The tail section of Air India flight AI171 in the wreckage of the Ahmedabad building the aircraft struck after take-off in June 2025. The investigation into the crash, which killed 260 people, is in its final stage, the government told the Supreme Court.
carousel.nri_angle: AI171 was an Ahmedabad-London flight carrying many diaspora families; its final report is the document relatives in India, the UK and North America have waited 17 months for.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: At Ahmedabad's Narendra Modi Stadium, Diljit Dosanjh Calls Out 'Double Standards' Over Concert Complaints
carousel.excerpt: The Punjabi star used his Aura World Tour stop at the world's largest cricket stadium to ask why Coldplay's lyrics draw no objections while his shows face repeated complaints — and answered his critics with two words.
carousel.nri_angle: Dosanjh's stadium run links Wembley's diaspora crowd to a home-turf milestone, and his remarks speak to debates Punjabi audiences follow on both sides.

carousel.title: Deaf Graduate's AI Alarm SIVO.GO Wins UK James Dyson Award and £5,000
carousel.excerpt: Gargi Agrawalla, 23, built SIVO.GO from her own experience of missing alarms with her cochlear implant off; it turns fire alarms and doorbells into light and vibration.
carousel.image_caption: Gargi Agrawalla holds the components of SIVO.GO, the AI alert device she designed as her final-year project at Loughborough University. The device won the UK James Dyson Award, carrying a £5,000 prize fund for its next stage of development.
carousel.nri_angle: An Indian-origin designer in the UK turned her own experience of deafness into an award-winning safety device — the kind of diaspora engineering story that starts in a dorm room and aims at every hotel room.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Rupee Closes Above 93 for First Time in Seven Months, at 92.67 to the Dollar
carousel.excerpt: A fifth straight session of gains, powered by ₹84,290 crore of foreign equity inflows in nine November sessions and weaker crude, took the rupee past a level it last closed above on April 10.
carousel.image_caption: A graphic shows the US dollar and Indian rupee symbols side by side.
carousel.nri_angle: A rupee at 92.67 means each dollar remitted to India converts to fewer rupees than a week ago, while a sustained rally would ease India's import bill.
